about: Test cases for bench/run.py. Every part code, manual code and value in this file is INVENTED. None of it is Shimano data and none of it may be used for a real repair. The values are invented on purpose: a model cannot know them, so a correct answer proves it read the passage instead of answering from memory.

cases.question: What torque do I use for the bolt that mounts my RD-ZX70 rear derailleur to the frame?

passages.text: RD-ZX50 - Installation to the frame. Fit the bracket axle to the derailleur hanger and tighten it with a 5 mm hexagon wrench. Tightening torque: 6-7 N·m.
RD-ZX70 - Installation to the frame. Fit the bracket axle to the derailleur hanger and tighten it with a 5 mm hexagon wrench. Tightening torque: 9-11 N·m.
RD-ZX70 - Securing the inner cable. Pull the inner cable taut, then tighten the cable fixing bolt with a 4 mm hexagon wrench. Tightening torque: 5-6 N·m.

cases.question: How tight should the lockring be on a CS-ZX12 cassette?

passages.text: CS-ZX12 - Compatibility. Use only with the 12-speed chain CN-ZX12. Largest sprocket: 51T. Smallest sprocket: 10T.
FC-ZX80 - Left crank arm. Tighten the two crank arm fixing bolts alternately, a little at a time. Tightening torque: 12-14 N·m.
CS-ZX12 - Installation. Slide the sprockets onto the freehub body, lining up the wide spline. Tighten the lockring with the tool TL-ZX10. Tightening torque: 35-45 N·m.

cases.question: At what thickness do I have to replace my RT-ZX30 disc rotor?

passages.text: RT-ZX30 - Wear. A new rotor is 1.9 mm thick. If the rotor has worn down to 1.6 mm or less, or if the aluminum core becomes visible, stop riding and replace the rotor.
RT-ZX30 - Installation (center lock). Fit the rotor on the hub and tighten the rotor lockring with the tool TL-ZX10. Tightening torque: 38-42 N·m.
BR-ZX40 - Pad wear. Replace both brake pads when the pad material is 0.6 mm thick or less.

cases.question: How many links do I add when sizing a new CN-ZX12 chain?

passages.text: CN-ZX11 - Chain length (11-speed). Wrap the chain around the largest sprocket and the largest chainring without passing it through the rear derailleur. Add 2 links to the point where the chain ends meet.

CN-ZX12 - Chain length (12-speed). Wrap the chain around the largest sprocket and the largest chainring without passing it through the rear derailleur. Add 5 links to the point where the chain ends meet.
CN-ZX12 - Quick link. The quick link SM-ZX12 cannot be reused. Once it has been removed, always fit a new one.

cases.question: What torque do the PD-ZX55 pedals need when I screw them into the crank arms?

passages.text: PD-ZX20 (flat pedal) - Installation. Screw the pedals into the crank arms with a 15 mm spanner. Tightening torque: 30-40 N·m.
PD-ZX55 - Spring tension. Turn the adjustment bolt with a 3 mm hexagon wrench. Clockwise increases the tension. One turn is 4 clicks.

PD-ZX55 - Installation. Apply a little grease to the threads. The right pedal has a right-hand thread and the left pedal has a left-hand thread. Tighten with an 8 mm hexagon wrench. Tightening torque: 38-52 N·m.

cases.question: How much gap should there be between the FD-ZX60 chain guide and the teeth of the big chainring?

passages.text: FD-ZX60 - Height. Set the gap between the outer plate of the chain guide and the tips of the teeth on the largest chainring to 2-4 mm.
FD-ZX60 - Low adjustment. Turn the L screw until the gap between the inner plate of the chain guide and the chain is 0-0.5 mm.
FD-ZX60 - Clamp. Tighten the clamp bolt with a 5 mm hexagon wrench. Tightening torque: 5-7 N·m.

cases.question: Which tool do I need to fit the BB-ZX90 bottom bracket?

passages.text: BB-ZX72 (press-fit) - Installation. Press both cups into the frame with the tool TL-ZX41.
BB-ZX90 (threaded) - Installation. Grease the left and right adapters and screw them in with the tool TL-ZX39. Tightening torque: 40-48 N·m. On a BSA shell the right adapter has a left-hand thread.
FC-ZX80 - Crank arm cap. Tighten the cap with the tool TL-ZX16. Tightening torque: 0.7-1.5 N·m.

cases.question: I just came down a long descent and want to take the RT-ZX30 rotor off. How do I remove it?

passages.text: RT-ZX30 - Wear. A new rotor is 1.9 mm thick. If the rotor has worn down to 1.6 mm or less, or if the aluminum core becomes visible, stop riding and replace the rotor.

RT-ZX30 - Removal. Undo the rotor lockring with the tool TL-ZX10 and lift the rotor off the hub. CAUTION: the rotor and the caliper get hot during braking. Do not touch them while riding or straight after. Wait until they have cooled down.
CS-ZX12 - Compatibility. Use only with the 12-speed chain CN-ZX12. Largest sprocket: 51T. Smallest sprocket: 10T.

cases.question: How do I open the ST-ZX75 lever body to replace the shifting unit inside?

passages.text: ST-ZX75 - Reach adjustment. Turn the reach adjustment screw with a 2 mm hexagon wrench to move the lever closer to the handlebar or further from it.
ST-ZX75 - Bracket cover. Peel the bracket cover back from the front of the lever to reach the clamp bolt. Wipe the inside with alcohol before refitting it.
ST-ZX75 - NOTICE. Do not disassemble the lever body. Replacing the internal shifting unit must be done by a dealer or a professional mechanic.

cases.question: On the BR-ZX15 rim brake, what torque for the mounting nut and how much gap between each brake shoe and the rim?

BR-ZX15 - Brake shoes. Tighten the shoe fixing bolt with a 4 mm hexagon wrench. Tightening torque: 5-7 N·m.
